sections.title: Listening. Listen to Dilnoza talking to her friend about a trip. Choose the correct answers.
sections.script:
Jasur: Hi Dilnoza! How was your trip to the mountains?
Dilnoza: Amazing, but also a bit frightening! We were climbing to a lake at about three thousand metres.
Jasur: Wow. Did you get there?
Dilnoza: Yes, in the end. But while we were walking up the last part, a thick fog came down. We couldn't see more than five metres.
Jasur: That sounds dangerous. What did you do?
Dilnoza: Our guide told us to stop and wait. We sat on our rucksacks for about an hour and drank hot tea from a flask.
Jasur: Were you cold?
Dilnoza: Freezing! I had a warm jacket, but I forgot my gloves.
Jasur: And then?
Dilnoza: The fog disappeared and suddenly we saw the lake. It was absolutely stunning — bright blue, like a mirror.
Jasur: Would you go again?
Dilnoza: Definitely. But next time I'll pack better!

o: To a lake in the mountains
To the top of a volcano

items.q: What was the problem during the climb?
What did the group do?
o: They waited for about an hour.

items.q: What did Dilnoza forget?
How did she feel when she saw the lake?

sections.title: G. Read the text and choose the correct answers.
sections.passage:
In 2016 a young Uzbek climber, Bobur, tried to climb Khan Tengri, a 7,010-metre mountain on the border of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. He trained for two years, running in the Chimgan hills every morning.

On the third day of the climb, while he was crossing a glacier, a snowstorm hit the mountain. Bobur couldn’t see more than two metres in front of him. Instead of continuing, he built a small wall of snow, got into his sleeping bag and waited. He spent eighteen hours there, eating chocolate and melting snow for water.

When the storm finished, he was cold and tired, and he decided to go down. ‘The mountain will still be there next year,’ he wrote in his diary. A year later he went back and reached the top. Today he gives talks at schools. ‘The most important skill in adventure,’ he tells students, ‘is knowing when to stop.’

items.q: What did Bobur do during the snowstorm?
o: He stopped and waited in a snow shelter.

items.q: Why did Bobur go down after the storm?
What does Bobur tell students?
o: You must always reach the top.
It is important to know when to stop.

items.q: What is the writer’s purpose?
o: To tell the story of a climber who made a good decision.
To explain how glaciers are formed.

items.q: Bobur reached the top of Khan Tengri on his first attempt.
